checks.label: For a function that multiplies by 3 and subtracts one, the inverse function is add one and then divide by 3: the first screen's facing machine runs + 1 then ÷ 3, turns 14 into 15 and then 5, and hands back every start tried from −6 to 10

Not all functions possess an inverse function; only one-to-one functions do: the square sends 3 and −3 to the same 9 and the root hands back 3 both times, while with the lock (0 and up) −3 is kept out and every start tried from 0 to 10 comes back

A horizontal line drawn on the graph that cuts it more than once means two different inputs have yielded the same output: the level line at 9 cuts the square twice, at −3 and 3, the one at 4 twice, at −2 and 2, while the cube's level lines at 8 and −8 cut it once each
√0.5 = 0.707, so a 12 mA signal from the DP cell is 50% DP but 71% flow rate: the lock screen's flow meter line reads √0.5 = 0.707, so 71% of full flow
The DP is proportional to the square of the flow, so the system must scale flow from the square root of the DP: for every flow from 0 to 1 of full, the root of its square gives the flow back

Each real-world value is converted with the linear equation y = mx + b: S(p) = 0.16p + 4 sends 0% to 4 mA and 100% to 20 mA, its 16 mA span over 100% is 0.16 mA per percent, and its undoing machine takes 12 mA to 50%, 16 mA to 75% and every reading from 4 to 20 mA back to its percentage

Graph functions and their inverse functions: the closing screen plots f(x) = 3x − 1 and its inverse on one grid, (5, 14) on f lands on (14, 5) on the inverse, and every point tried on f, its two numbers swapped, lies on the inverse

On every machine screen, and after every answer, each number drawn is what its step makes of the number before it, the first machine working top to bottom and the facing one bottom to top; an answer dropped into the input runs forwards to the number given

Each step in a facing machine is the opposite of the one beside it: run through it, the number between its steps matches the first machine's at the same height and the start comes back, on screens 1, 3, 5 and 7; undone in the same order, 14 gives 10 and then 5, not 3

Each puzzle accepts only its own answer, and after each wrong pick the picture shows the slip making exactly that answer: stopping halfway, running the machine forwards again, undoing in the same order, reading −1 as a power, forgetting the 4 mA, or taking the root first
Before an answer, nothing in a puzzle's picture gives it away: only the number given is drawn, the places still to fill wait empty or as question marks, and no level line shows

Every demonstration has settled within 4.6 s of its screen opening, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends, and the same-order switch within 4 s; every answer's motion, right or wrong, within 3 s

Every worked number is right (5 → 15 → 14 and back; 8 → 9 → 3, 23 forwards; 3 → 7 → 14 and back, 10 and 5 the same order; 20 → 10 → 6, 16 and 8 the same order, 48 forwards; 10 ÷ 2 = 5, 1 ÷ f(10) = 0.05, 20 doubled; 50% → 8 → 12 mA and back; 16 mA → 12 → 75%, 100% without the 4 mA, 96% the same order; 3 and −3 → 9 → 3; 100 W → 25 → 5 A, root first 10 then 2.5; 2³ = 8, (−2)³ = −8, 2² = (−2)² = 4; 8 mA → 4 → 25%)
